title: --text-5 fails WCAG in BOTH themes — 275 inline-style usages
fix: Darken the light value and lighten the dark value so each clears 4.5:1 on its own darkest/lightest ground. Light: #9ca3af -> #64748b gives 4.76:1 on #ffffff but only 4.31:1 on --bg-base #f0f4f9, so go to #5b6675 (~5.5:1 on #f0f4f9) or #6b7280 (4.83:1 on white). Dark: #475569 -> #7c8ba1 gives ~5.2:1 on #0f1117. Because --text-5 is the bottom of the ramp it must still sit visually below --text-4, so --text-4 has to move at the same time (see the --text-4 finding).
effect: On the daily Home, Dashboard, Requests, Agents, Clients and Calendar screens, all secondary copy — empty-state messages ('No tickets in the last 24 hours', 'Your personal notes appear here'), relative timestamps, weekday headers, field labels, 10px section headings — renders at 2.3:1 in light mode (pale grey #9ca3af on the near-white #f0f4f9 page, reads as washed out to blank) and 2.5:1 in dark mode (dull #475569 on near-black, reads as barely-there). This is literally both halves of the user's reported symptom.

title: --text-4 is byte-identical #64748b in light and dark and fails 4.5:1 in both
fix: Give it distinct per-theme values. Light: #64748b -> #556070 (~5.6:1 on #f0f4f9, ~6.2:1 on white), keeping it clearly lighter than --text-3 #475569. Dark: #64748b -> #94a3b8 would collide with --text-3's dark value, so use #8593a8 (~6.0:1 on #0f1117) and push --text-3 dark slightly lighter, or accept a 4-step ramp. Verify against --bg-hover in light (#e2e8f0) and --bg-card in dark (#1a1d27), which are the worst-case grounds.
effect: In dark mode #64748b never clears 4.5:1 on any app surface (3.5:1 on panels), so at 11px the 'View all' ghost buttons on Home, the pagination counter and 'N total tickets' footer on the ticket list, agent role labels and calendar event metadata all read as dull, muddy grey. In light mode the same token sits at 3.9-4.3:1 on the page and hover grounds, so the identical text is faint there too — the token cannot serve both grounds and is the second-largest contributor to the reported symptom after --text-5.

title: Pre-hydration splash is hardcoded dark — light-mode users see a near-black full-screen splash
evidence:
background: '#0E1117',          // layout.tsx:102, #app-splash
            color: '#ECEEF2', lineHeight: 1, // layout.tsx:164, MD wordmark
            color: '#ECEEF2', lineHeight: 1, // layout.tsx:182, MC wordmark
            color: '#374151', letterSpacing: '0.1em', // layout.tsx:193 and :202, subtitles
fix: Swap the four literals for tokens, which are already resolved at this point because next-themes writes data-theme on <html> from a blocking script before paint: line 102 `background: '#0E1117'` -> `'var(--bg-base)'`; lines 164 and 182 `color: '#ECEEF2'` -> `'var(--text-0)'`; lines 193 and 202 `color: '#374151'` -> `'var(--text-3)'` (not --text-4/--text-5, both of which fail contrast per the other findings). Leave the brand blues (#1F4ED8) and MC greens (#10b981) hardcoded — those are intentionally theme-invariant.
effect: A user whose stored theme is light gets a full-screen #0E1117 black brand splash for ~1s on every hard load/reload before it fades to the near-white app — a jarring flash, but the splash content itself is legible. Separately, in both themes the 'Loading workspace…' / 'RMM Platform' subtitle at layout.tsx:193/:202 renders #374151 on #0E1117 at 1.83:1 and is effectively invisible.

title: --bg-hover and --border-subtle are the SAME hex in both themes, erasing table row separators on hover
evidence:
--bg-hover:      #e2e8f0;   /* light, globals.css:95 */
    --border-subtle: #e2e8f0;   /* light, globals.css:98 */
    --bg-hover:      #1e2130;   /* dark,  globals.css:42 */
    --border-subtle: #1e2130;   /* dark,  globals.css:46 */
fix: Separate the two ramps. Light: keep --border-subtle #e2e8f0 and move --bg-hover to #eaeff5 (a hover tint lighter than the border) or push --border-subtle to #d7dfe9 and keep the hover. Dark: keep --border-subtle #1e2130 and move --bg-hover to #232739. Either direction works as long as the two are no longer equal in either block.
effect: On the ticket / organization / client / KB tables, hovering a row makes that row's own 1px bottom rule dissolve into its highlight band, so the hovered row appears to merge with the row below it. Purely cosmetic; nothing becomes unreadable.

title: .input::placeholder is bound to --text-5, giving ~2.2-2.4:1 placeholder text
evidence:
.input::placeholder { color: var(--text-5); }   /* globals.css:240 */
  .input { background: var(--bg-elevated); ... }  /* globals.css:237 */
fix: Do not point placeholders at the bottom of the ramp. Change globals.css:240 to `color: var(--text-4);` once --text-4 is corrected per the finding above, or introduce a dedicated --text-placeholder token defined in both blocks at ~4.6:1 against --bg-elevated (light ~#6a7686 on #eef2f7, dark ~#8494a8 on #252936).
effect: On the Requests ticket list, the search field's 'Search tickets… (Enter)' placeholder renders at 2.43:1 in light mode and 2.19:1 in dark, so the box reads as empty and unlabelled; same for the KB documentation search and the appearance-settings inputs.

title: --border-md renders at 1.48:1 light / 1.25:1 dark — 483 usages
fix: Light: #cbd5e1 -> #b6c2d1 (~2.0:1) is still short; to actually clear 3:1 on white the border must be ~#98a6b8. If that reads too heavy for a chrome-dense UI, accept 2:1 for decorative panel edges but raise it to 3:1 specifically for .input (globals.css:237) and .btn-secondary (211), which are interactive controls where 1.4.11 genuinely applies. Dark: #2a2f3d -> #3a4256 gives ~2.0:1 on #1a1d27; #454e66 reaches ~3:1.
effect: Panel outlines, the table header rule and input borders are near-invisible hairlines, so the light theme reads flat — panels barely separate from the #f0f4f9 page (which is itself only ~1.05:1 from --bg-card #f8fafc). A perceived-flatness/polish issue, not a legibility failure, and no text is affected.

title: Google Fonts @import duplicates the next/font loads already declared in layout.tsx
fix: Delete globals.css:1, then change globals.css:338 and :339 from `font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace` to `font-family: var(--font-mono), monospace` so they use the self-hosted next/font face.
effect: An extra render-blocking third-party request to fonts.googleapis.com on first load, re-downloading two font families Next.js already self-hosts. Latent: the TipTap editor's code-block and inline-code font at globals.css:338-339 depends on that remote fetch, so it would silently fall back to the generic monospace if the @import were removed.

title: Reply composer tab labels hardcode #ffffff over a 18%-alpha tint — invisible in light mode
evidence:
? { background: 'rgba(37,99,235,0.18)', color: '#ffffff', fontSize: 13, borderRight: isMSP ? '1px solid var(--border-md)' : 'none' }
: { background: 'transparent', color: 'var(--text-4)', fontSize: 13, borderRight: ... }
fix: Replace the literal with the token that already inverts correctly: color: 'var(--text-0)' for both selected branches (line 1266 and 1276). --text-0 is #f8fafc in dark and #0f172a in light, so the selected label stays legible in both. Do not keep '#ffffff' — the tinted background is theme-dependent, so the foreground must be too.
effect: On the ticket detail page in light mode, the active segment of the Public Reply / Internal Note toggle renders its label and icon in white on a pale blue (or pale amber) fill and is unreadable; the inactive segment stays crisp. The user can still tell which tab is selected from the fill, but cannot read its name.

title: Every message timestamp in the ticket thread hardcodes #e2e8f0 — 1.18:1 on the light card
fix: color: 'var(--text-1)' — this is an exact token swap, since --text-1 is #e2e8f0 in dark mode, so dark-mode rendering is pixel-identical while light mode gains #1e293b.
effect: On the ticket detail page in light mode, the date/time line under every message author renders near-white on the white message card and is invisible; a 20-reply thread shows 20 blank timestamp rows while author name and body read normally.

title: Merge/Absorb card emphasis words hardcode #ffffff on var(--bg-card) — invisible in light mode
evidence: Merge — this ticket is a duplicate; close it into another.
fix: color: 'var(--text-0)' on both spans. --text-0 is #f8fafc in dark (visually equivalent to the current #ffffff) and #0f172a in light, preserving the intended 'brighter than body text' emphasis in both themes.
effect: On the ticket detail page in light mode (MSP roles only), the Merge / Absorb sidebar card's two bolded lead words vanish, leaving '____ — this ticket is a duplicate; close it into another.' with a hole where the label should be.

title: Dashboard 'Unassigned' KPI value hardcodes #94a3b8 on a pure-white surface — 2.54:1
fix: Line 232 and line 292: color: 'var(--text-3)' (#94a3b8 dark, #475569 light) — dark mode is unchanged, light mode reaches ~7:1. For line 43's statCards entry, the config object needs a token string ('var(--text-3)') rather than a hex if it is only ever used as a CSS color value.
effect: On /dashboard in light mode, the 20px Unassigned count renders as pale grey on white, and the activity-feed message previews in the page's largest panel render as 12px pale grey on the near-white card — both readable only with effort, matching the reported 'washed out' complaint.

title: Active nav item label #60a5fa over rgba(37,99,235,0.1) — 2.13:1 in light mode on every screen
fix: Use a darker accent for the active state that survives both grounds, e.g. color: isActive ? 'var(--primary-strong)' : 'var(--text-2)' backed by a new token (#60a5fa dark / #1d4ed8 light), or at minimum raise the active background alpha and switch to hsl(var(--primary)) with a light-mode override. The literal #60a5fa cannot work against both #1a1d27 and #ffffff.
effect: In light mode the sidebar entry for the page you are currently on renders light blue on pale blue, noticeably fainter than every inactive entry (which sits at #334155) — the active item looks disabled rather than selected.

title: MATECONNECT launcher label #4ade80 on rgba(16,185,129,0.1) — 1.53:1 in light mode
fix: Replace #4ade80 at lines 184, 204 and 213 with a token pair that darkens in light mode (e.g. var(--accent-connect), #4ade80 dark / #047857 light). Green at that lightness cannot clear 4.5:1 on white at any weight.
effect: In light mode, for MSP users with MateConnect enabled and the sidebar expanded, the launcher at the bottom of the nav reads 'MATE' followed by blank space — the 'CONNECT' half of the product name is invisible on the pale green pill.

title: Role badge palette hardcodes #94a3b8 for End User — 2.5:1 on the light badge fill
fix: These config maps need per-theme values, not a single hex. Either move each pair into globals.css as token pairs (--badge-enduser-fg / --badge-enduser-bg defined in both :root and [data-theme="light"]) and reference var() from the config, or darken the foreground hexes by ~2 steps and raise the fill alpha so the pair clears 4.5:1 on white.
effect: On any user profile in light mode the 'End User' role chip renders pale grey on near-white; in the same page's recent-tickets table the Priority column text (green 'Low', amber 'High') is drawn with no background tint and is close to invisible on the white row.

title: Image-attach button flips to hardcoded #ffffff when files are attached — invisible in light mode
fix: Line 1294: color: replyImages.length > 0 ? 'var(--text-0)' : 'var(--text-2)'. Leave line 1592 as-is — white on solid #2563eb is correct in both themes; only the alpha-tinted backgrounds are the problem.
effect: On the ticket detail page in light mode, the moment you attach an image the button's own label ('1 image') and icon turn white on a pale lavender fill and disappear — the confirmation of the attachment count is unreadable exactly when it matters.

title: Profile dropdown role and status badges use accent-on-own-tint — washed out in light mode
fix: Introduce light-mode-aware accent tokens for badge foregrounds (e.g. --accent-info-fg: #60a5fa dark / #1d4ed8 light; --accent-ok-fg: #34d399 dark / #047857 light) and reference them at lines 121 and 131. Line 227's #f87171 on the sign-out row needs the same treatment (~3.0:1 on white).
effect: Opening the profile panel from the topbar in light mode, the role chip ('MSP Owner' etc.) and the green 'Online' chip render as barely-there text on pale fills, while every other line in the panel (name, email, menu items) is crisply dark.

title: Home statCards seed #94a3b8 for the Unassigned tile — pale grey on white
evidence: { label: 'Unassigned',         value: stats?.unassigned    ?? 0, color: '#94a3b8', icon: Users         },
fix: Give the neutral stat its own token pair rather than the raw dark-mode text colour: color: 'var(--text-3)' resolves to #94a3b8 in dark and #475569 in light, keeping the tile visually neutral while staying legible.
effect: On /home in light mode the Unassigned tile's number reads slightly washed grey on the near-white card — but so do several sibling tiles (Due Today in amber is worse), so no single tile stands out as broken.

title: Ticket list status/priority badge palette is dark-mode-only — ~2.0:1 on every row in light mode
fix: Hoist these four maps into a single shared module and express each colour as a var() referencing token pairs defined in both :root and [data-theme="light"] in globals.css (e.g. --status-open-fg: #60a5fa / #1d4ed8, --status-open-bg: rgba(59,130,246,0.15) / rgba(29,78,216,0.12)). Duplicating the maps across three files is why the drift exists.
effect: On the requests list in light mode every row's Status, Priority and SLA chips render as low-contrast tinted smudges (blue-on-pale-blue, amber-on-pale-amber) against otherwise crisp dark row text, so the list's only colour-coded columns are the hardest to read — and the same chips repeat at the top of the ticket detail page.

title: Chart tooltip text hex is identical to its own light-mode background hex (1.0:1 contrast)
fix: Replace '#e2e8f0' with 'var(--text-1)'. The .chart-tooltip rule already sets color: var(--text-1) on the container, so the inline override can simply be deleted and the value will inherit correctly in both themes.
effect: On /dashboard in light mode, hovering a slice of the Priority donut shows a tooltip whose numeric value is painted #e2e8f0 on an #e2e8f0 background and is completely invisible; the donut legend's per-priority counts and the Total figure beside the chart are likewise near-white on the near-white panel and cannot be read at all.

title: App-wide event alert bar paints a near-opaque black background under tokenised text
fix: Replace the hardcoded bg pair with a token-based surface, e.g. bg = 'var(--bg-elevated)' with the accent carried by the existing borderLeft/borderTop, or define --bg-alert-critical / --bg-alert-warn in both :root and [data-theme="light"] blocks of globals.css and reference those.
effect: In light mode, when a user has an imminent or overdue assigned event, a near-black bar appears pinned to the bottom of every dashboard page; the event title inside it renders dark slate on near-black at ~2.4:1 and is very hard to read, while the surrounding countdown and status label stay legible.

title: Notification row hover sets a near-black background while row text stays tokenised
fix: Change the hover value to 'var(--bg-hover)' and the onMouseLeave restore at line 163 accordingly; both already have tokens available on this element.
effect: In light mode, opening the notification panel from the topbar and moving the mouse over any unread notification makes that row's message text vanish entirely (dark navy text on a near-black hover fill) until the pointer moves away.

title: Reply-type tabs paint pure white text on a 13-18% colour tint
evidence: ? { background: 'rgba(37,99,235,0.18)', color: '#ffffff', fontSize: 13, borderRight: isMSP ? '1px solid var(--border-md)' : 'none' }
fix: Swap color:'#ffffff' for 'var(--text-0)' on all three, or give the active tab a solid accent fill (background:'#2563eb' with color:'#fff') so the white text has a real surface to sit on in both themes.
effect: On the ticket detail page in light mode, the label of whichever reply mode is active ('Public Reply' or 'Internal Note') renders pure white on a pale blue/amber tint and is unreadable, so the user cannot tell whether they are about to send a customer-visible reply or a private internal note; the image-attach button's label disappears the same way once an image is attached.

title: Requests list status/priority/SLA badge maps hardcode dark-theme tint+text pairs
fix: Replace the three maps with theme-aware values driven by the existing .badge-* classes (className={`badge-${status}`}), or add [data-theme="light"] variants mirroring globals.css:284-292 — 10% tint with 600/700-weight text such as #1d4ed8, #92400e, #047857, #991b1b.
effect: On the /requests list in light mode, every row's Status, Priority and SLA badge renders a pale 400-weight colour on an almost-white tint at 1.4-2.1:1; 'In Progress', 'High', 'On Track' and 'Due Soon' are effectively unreadable, so the user cannot triage the queue at a glance.

title: Notification Settings page hardcodes near-white text on tokenised .panel surfaces
fix: Map the four hardcoded values to tokens: '#e2e8f0' -> 'var(--text-1)', '#64748b' -> 'var(--text-4)', '#252936' -> 'var(--bg-elevated)', '#1e2130' -> 'var(--border-subtle)'.
effect: On /settings/notifications in light mode the heading 'Notification Settings' and the label of every individual notification toggle render near-white on a near-white panel and are unreadable, leaving the user with a column of unlabelled switches separated by harsh near-black rules.

title: Active nav item and MateConnect link use rgba tints with light-only accent text
fix: Use a theme-aware accent: keep the tint but switch text to a token pair, e.g. color: isActive ? 'var(--primary-accent-text)' : 'var(--text-2)' with --primary-accent-text defined as #60a5fa on :root and #1d4ed8 on [data-theme="light"]; apply the same treatment to the green MateConnect accent (#4ade80 -> #15803d in light).
effect: In light mode the sidebar item for the page you are currently on is the hardest one to read (pale blue label and icon on a near-white tint, ~2.2:1), so the user loses their sense of place on every screen; for permitted users the MATECONNECT link at the bottom has its 'CONNECT' half nearly erased at ~1.6:1.

title: Appearance/theme settings page itself washes out in light mode
fix: Raise the tint to a token surface (var(--bg-elevated)) and switch '#93c5fd'/'#60a5fa' to 'var(--text-2)' or a theme-aware accent token defined per mode in globals.css.
effect: On /settings/appearance in light mode the 'Browser-local settings' explanatory heading is pale blue on near-white and unreadable, and the currently-selected zoom / tickets-per-page chip is only faintly distinguishable from the unselected ones, so the user cannot see which preset is active.

title: Role and Online badges in the profile panel use tint+light-hex pairs
fix: Switch the three text hexes to mode-aware values (light: #1d4ed8, #047857, #b91c1c) via tokens, mirroring the [data-theme="light"] badge treatment already present at globals.css:284-292.
effect: In light mode, opening the profile panel shows the user's role badge and the green 'Online' badge as barely-there text on pale tints (1.5-1.8:1, essentially unreadable), and the red 'Sign out' label sits at ~2.2:1 against the pale panel.

title: Undefined --bg-panel token leaves KB editor chrome with no background in either theme
evidence: <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1 p-2 border-b border-[var(--border-subtle)] bg-[var(--bg-panel)] flex-shrink-0">
fix: Either define --bg-panel and --bg-input in both the :root and [data-theme="light"] blocks of globals.css, or repoint the 14 call sites at existing tokens (--bg-surface for panels, --bg-elevated for inputs).
effect: In both themes, the KB editor's slash-command menu, doc-link picker, selection bubble menu and find-and-replace popover render with no background at all, so the document text underneath shows through the menu items and the menus are unreadable; the KB documentation side panels and the To/CC/BCC email fields on the ticket page also lose their intended surface and blend into whatever is behind them.

title: Full-screen navigation overlay is hardcoded near-black on every route change
fix: Replace '#0E1117' with 'var(--bg-base)'.
effect: In light mode every click on a sidebar link or profile-menu link flashes a full-screen near-black overlay for a few hundred milliseconds before the new page appears, so navigating the app strobes between white and black and reads as the theme failing.

title: Every form input on the Organizations settings page is a hardcoded dark field
evidence: const inp = 'w-full h-9 px-3 text-[13px] bg-[#0f1117] border border-[#2a2f3d] text-[#e2e8f0] placeholder-[#3d4a6b] outline-none focus:border-[#2563eb] transition-colors';
fix: Rewrite inp/lbl against tokens: bg-[var(--bg-elevated)] border-[var(--border-md)] text-[var(--text-1)] placeholder-[var(--text-5)], and delete the inline <option> background at line 340 so the native control follows the page theme.
effect: In light mode, opening the create/edit organization modal on /settings/organizations shows a white dialog containing a stack of near-black input slabs, and each field's uppercase label ('Organization Name', 'Domain', 'Email'…) renders light grey on white at ~2.45:1, making the form hard to read and visibly broken.

title: Home announcement cards use amber/violet tints with light-only accent text
fix: Route these through the theme-aware badge tokens (see globals.css:284-292) rather than inline tints, deepening both the tint alpha and the text weight/darkness under [data-theme="light"].
effect: On /home in light mode the announcement audience pills ('ALL' / 'SPECIFIC') and the 'Nd overdue' badges in the My Overdue column render pale amber/violet/red on near-white tints at roughly 1.9-2.4:1 and are hard or impossible to read, and the purple + button beside the notes input looks inactive.

title: Malformed boxShadow nests a full shadow value inside a shadow shorthand, dropping it entirely
fix: Change to boxShadow: 'var(--shadow-panel)' to match ProfileDropdown.tsx:70.
effect: The notification slide-in panel has no drop shadow in either theme, so it reads as slightly flatter against the page than the profile panel next to it; it remains clearly delineated by its left border and the backdrop dimming.

title: Day-group and row dividers hardcode a near-black border inside a tokenised panel
fix: Replace both occurrences of '#111527' with 'var(--border-panel)'.
effect: In light mode the notification panel is ruled by harsh near-black 1px lines between each date group and each notification row instead of the pale separators the rest of the panel uses, which looks unfinished but does not obscure any content.

title: Shared tooltip primitive is hardcoded dark and never flips
fix: Switch to tokens: bg-[var(--bg-elevated)] border-[var(--border-md)] text-[var(--text-1)].
effect: In light mode, users who collapse the sidebar see each nav icon's hover tooltip render as a near-black chip with white text floating over the white UI — legible, but visibly the wrong theme.

title: severityBg returns hardcoded tints paired with light-only severityColor text
fix: Return theme-aware values — either CSS variables defined per mode in globals.css, or darken the text side under light (#a16207 for yellow, #15803d for green, #c2410c for orange) alongside a stronger tint.
effect: In light mode every MateConnect severity badge washes out — on /mateconnect/alerts and the MC dashboard the 'MEDIUM' and 'LOW' labels are yellow/green on near-white tints at 1.4-1.6:1 and cannot be read, so the user cannot tell alert severities apart; 'HIGH' is barely legible and only 'CRITICAL' survives.

title: Pre-hydration splash screen is hardcoded near-black for light-mode users
fix: Extend the SPLASH_BOOT script to read the next-themes value from localStorage and set the splash background to #f0f4f9 when light, mirroring how it already sets html[data-splash="mc"].
effect: A light-mode user's every cold page load opens with a full-screen near-black splash carrying the MateDesk wordmark, which then fades to a white app — the app appears to boot in the wrong theme each time.

title: Modal scrims hardcode heavy black alpha, far too dark for light mode
evidence: style={{ position: 'fixed', inset: 0, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.65)', zIndex: 200, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}
fix: Introduce a --scrim token (e.g. rgba(0,0,0,0.65) on :root, rgba(15,23,42,0.35) on [data-theme="light"]) in globals.css and replace the inline rgba(0,0,0,x) scrim literals with var(--scrim).
effect: In light mode, opening any modal or drawer dims the page to near-black behind it, which is heavier than a light theme normally warrants and momentarily reads as the app switching to dark; nothing becomes unreadable.

title: Logout confirmation page is entirely hardcoded dark
fix: Replace '#0f1117' with 'var(--bg-base)' and the three text hexes with 'var(--text-4)', 'var(--text-3)' and 'var(--text-5)'.
effect: A light-mode user who signs out gets a roughly 800ms full-screen black 'Signing you out…' page before landing on the login screen — readable, but a jarring theme break at the end of the session.

title: Pre-hydration splash overlay is hardcoded dark and covers the whole viewport on every load, regardless of theme
effect: On every hard page load / refresh, a light-mode user gets a full-viewport near-black splash for ~700ms-1s before their light UI appears. Additionally the 'Loading workspace…' subtitle (#374151 on #0E1117, ~1.85:1) is unreadable on the splash in both modes.

title: Page-transition overlay hardcodes dark #0E1117 and is mounted outside ThemeProvider so it cannot read the theme
evidence:
<div
      aria-hidden
      style={{
        position: 'fixed',
        inset: 0,
        zIndex: 9998,
        background: '#0E1117',
fix: Change background to 'var(--bg-base)' (the token already flips correctly), and move <SplashDismiss /> and <PageTransitionOverlay /> inside the ThemeProvider in layout.tsx so they sit in theme context: wrap lines 208-215 as <ThemeProvider ...>{children}<SplashDismiss /><PageTransitionOverlay /></ThemeProvider>.
effect: In light mode, clicking any main sidebar or topbar nav item flashes the entire screen near-black (#0E1117) for roughly half a second on every navigation.

title: Landing-page product preview mixes a theme-reactive token background with hardcoded near-white text — wordmark is invisible in light mode
evidence: MateDesk
fix: The public marketing site is intentionally always-light, so this mock chrome must not consume theme tokens. Replace 'var(--bg-surface)' on line 170 with the literal dark mock value '#151821' (matching the intended screenshot look and the '#e2e8f0' wordmark), or alternatively make the whole block light by using '#F7F8FA' background with '#0B1220' wordmark text to match the surrounding hero.
effect: On localhost (or any single-origin deploy) with light mode active, the 'MateDesk' wordmark in the hero's mock app sidebar renders #e2e8f0 on #ffffff and disappears. Not reproducible on the production marketing domain.

title: No `color-scheme` declared on :root or [data-theme="light"] — every native form control renders in the wrong mode
fix: Add `color-scheme: dark;` inside the :root block (after line 31) and `color-scheme: light;` inside the [data-theme="light"] block (after line 89). This is the single declaration that makes native popups, autofill and scrollbars follow data-theme.
effect: In dark mode the native number-input spinner arrows and the datetime picker icon on Settings > Appearance and New Request render as dark grey glyphs on the dark input and are nearly invisible; the calendar/time popups and Chrome autofill appear light-chromed inside dark panels.

title: MateConnect has no theme toggle anywhere — the MateDesk profile dropdown has one in the identical structural slot, MC does not
fix: Port the theme row from ProfileDropdown.tsx:169-210 into MCProfileDropdown.tsx between line 133 and 134 (after MENU_ITEMS, before Sign out), using next-themes useTheme() with MC.ACCENT for the ON state instead of '#2563eb'. If MC is to be split into a separate product, it needs its own ThemeProvider consumer rather than inheriting the toggle by accident.
effect: A user working inside /mateconnect/* has no way to change theme from anywhere in that module; MC appears locked into whatever mode was last set from the MateDesk side.

title: MateConnect "Appearance" settings page contains no theme control at all
evidence:
const SECTIONS = [
    {
      icon: RefreshCw,
      title: 'Data Refresh',
...
      icon: LayoutGrid,
      title: 'Device Table',
...
      icon: Monitor,
      title: 'Display Density',
fix: Add a 'Theme' section to SECTIONS using next-themes useTheme() with a mounted guard, wired to setTheme('light'|'dark'), so both appearance pages expose the same control. Longer term, since the SECTIONS list is a plain array of Rows, the theme row can reuse the existing OptionGroup component (line 42) with options [{label:'Dark',value:'dark'},{label:'Light',value:'light'}].
effect: An MC user who opens Settings > Appearance looking for light/dark finds only refresh interval, column toggles and density, and concludes theme switching is missing or broken.

title: MateConnect splash screen hardcodes dark background and near-white text on every client-side entry into MC
evidence:
style={{
        position: 'fixed', inset: 0, zIndex: 9999,
        background: '#0E1117',
        display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center',
fix: Replace '#0E1117' with var(--bg-base), '#ECEEF2' with var(--text-0), and '#374151' with var(--text-4). The green accent values (#10b981) are brand-fixed and should stay.
effect: In light mode, navigating from MateDesk into any /mateconnect/* route flashes a full-screen near-black branded splash for ~700ms-1.1s; its 'RMM Platform' subtitle is unreadable in both modes.

title: MateDesk "Appearance" page has no theme control; the app's only setTheme call is buried in a profile slide-over
fix: Add a Theme card to this page above the Zoom card, using next-themes useTheme() with a mounted guard (`const [mounted,setMounted]=useState(false); useEffect(()=>setMounted(true),[])`) so it does not render a wrong-state control before hydration, and call setTheme('light'|'dark'). Keep ProfileDropdown.tsx:189 as the quick toggle; both must go through setTheme so they stay in sync.
effect: A user looking for light/dark on Settings > Appearance finds only zoom and tickets-per-page; the working toggle is only reachable via the topbar avatar slide-over.

title: disableTransitionOnChange not set — toggling theme animates every transitioned element through washed-out intermediate colours
fix: Pass disableTransitionOnChange to ThemeProvider on line 208: <ThemeProvider attribute="data-theme" defaultTheme="dark" enableSystem={false} disableTransitionOnChange>. next-themes injects a temporary `* { transition: none !important }` style for one frame, making the swap instantaneous.
effect: When the theme is toggled, buttons and inputs crossfade their background/text over ~150ms while the rest of the page snaps immediately — a brief mismatched frame, self-correcting.

title: Saved zoom preference is only applied while the Appearance page is open — never restored on load
fix: Read matedesk_zoom in the same <head> boot script proposed for the theme (layout.tsx, next to SPLASH_BOOT) and apply document.documentElement.style.zoom before first paint, so zoom and theme are both restored by one pre-hydration pass.
effect: A user who sets interface zoom to e.g. 85% sees it applied immediately, then reverts to 100% after any refresh or on any other route, until they revisit Settings > Appearance.

title: Both Appearance pages write preferences that nothing ever reads — "Saved" confirms a no-op
fix: Either wire these keys into their consumers (MC device/alert polling and the Requests page query params), or remove the controls. Leaving a success toast on a write nothing reads trains users to distrust every settings page, including the theme control once it is added.
effect: Changing refresh interval, density or column visibility in MateConnect, or tickets-per-page in MateDesk, shows a success confirmation but changes nothing anywhere in the product.

title: Dashboard priority donut legend hardcodes near-white text — invisible on the light-mode panel
evidence: {d.name} {d.value}
fix: Replace the literals with the existing tokens that already have light values: line 51 -> color: 'var(--text-3)', lines 14/53/61 -> color: 'var(--text-1)'. No useTheme() needed since the tokens flip via [data-theme="light"].
effect: On the dashboard (first screen after login) in light mode, the 'Open Requests by Priority' donut legend shows only coloured dots — the priority names are washed out at 1.9:1 and every count number is invisible at 1.04:1, as is the 'Total' figure. Hovering a slice shows a tooltip whose value is 100% invisible (same hex as its background), so only 'High:' appears with no number.

title: TipTap injects a One-Dark hljs syntax palette with no light override, over a code block whose background flips to near-white
fix: Add a `[data-theme="light"] .hljs-*` block (GitHub-light values, e.g. keyword #cf222e, string #0a7d33, number #0550ae, title #6639ba, comment #6e7781) alongside these rules, or gate the whole injected <style> on resolvedTheme.
effect: On any KB documentation page containing a fenced code block, in light mode, the syntax-highlighted tokens render as pale One-Dark pastels on a near-white block: strings at 1.84:1 and numbers/keywords/titles at ~2.2:1 are effectively unreadable, so PowerShell/bash snippets in KB articles cannot be read without switching to dark mode.

title: --bg-panel is consumed in 11 places but is defined in neither the dark nor the light token block
evidence: <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1 p-2 border-b border-[var(--border-subtle)] bg-[var(--bg-panel)] flex-shrink-0">
fix: Add --bg-panel to both token blocks in globals.css (e.g. #151821 at line 43 and #ffffff at line 96), or repoint all 11 sites at the existing --bg-surface.
effect: In both themes, typing '/' in a KB document opens a slash-command menu that is a bordered, drop-shadowed but see-through box: the command names and subtitles overlap the article text underneath and are unreadable except for the one highlighted row. The same applies to the @-doc-link picker, the find-and-replace popup, the editor toolbar, and the KB three-pane sidebars, which lose their panel fill and merge into the canvas.

title: Page-transition overlay hardcodes a near-black full-screen backdrop on every navigation
fix: Use background: 'var(--bg-base)' so it follows the theme, and keep the arc colours (they are brand blues/greens that read on both).
effect: In light mode, clicking any sidebar link makes the entire viewport flash solid near-black (#0E1117) for roughly a quarter to half a second before the new light page appears — on every single navigation, which is the most frequently seen surface in the app.

title: Pre-hydration #app-splash hardcodes #0E1117 — light-mode users get a black full-screen splash on every hard load
fix: Extend SPLASH_BOOT to read the next-themes storage key and set a data-splash-theme attribute, then add `html[data-splash-theme="light"] #app-splash { background:#f0f4f9; }` (plus a dark wordmark colour) to SPLASH_CSS at layout.tsx:50-77.
effect: On a hard refresh or cold tab in light mode, the user sees a full-screen near-black branded splash for ~700ms before the light app paints — a jarring but transient brand moment. Independently, the 10px 'Loading workspace…' sub-label is illegible at 1.82:1 in every theme.

title: Badge light-mode overrides cover 9 of 9 defined classes — but the two classes the app actually uses are defined in neither theme
evidence:
[data-theme="light"] .badge-open     { background: rgba(37,99,235,0.10);   color: #1d4ed8; }
[data-theme="light"] .badge-pending  { background: rgba(79,70,229,0.10);   color: #4338ca; }
fix: Add `.badge` base plus `.badge-success` / `.badge-danger` to the @layer utilities block at line 270 with matching [data-theme="light"] overrides, or repoint the two settings pages at the existing badge-solved / badge-critical names.
effect: On Settings → Organizations (list and detail), the Status column renders 'Active' / 'Inactive' as plain body text with no pill background, no padding and no green/red semantic colour — identical in both themes, and readable, so a user must read the word rather than scan the colour.

title: The light-mode .ProseMirror code override out-specifies the pre-code reset, painting a blue chip over the whole code block
fix: Scope it to inline code only: `[data-theme="light"] .ProseMirror :not(pre) > code { … }`, or add a matching `[data-theme="light"] .ProseMirror pre code { background:none; color:inherit; }` reset.
effect: On KB documentation pages in light mode, fenced code blocks pick up a faint blue wash and any unhighlighted code text renders dark blue (#1d4ed8) instead of near-black — readable, but visibly inconsistent with the same block in dark mode.

title: Input placeholder is bound to --text-5, the palette's faintest step, failing contrast in both themes
fix: Bind the placeholder one step darker/lighter: `color: var(--text-4)` (#64748b both themes), which clears 3:1 against --bg-elevated in each mode without new tokens.
effect: On the Requests list page the 'Search tickets… (Enter)' placeholder is very faint in both themes — near-invisible in dark mode at 1.91:1 — as are the KB folder-name and image-URL dialog placeholders. Five fields total, and the field itself remains obvious from its border.

title: Every form placeholder in the product uses --text-5 on --bg-elevated: 1.91:1 dark, 2.26:1 light
fix: Use `--text-3` (dark 5.65:1, light 6.74:1 on --bg-elevated) for placeholders. If a dimmer placeholder is desired, `--text-3` is still the lowest step that clears 4.5:1 on --bg-elevated in both modes; --text-4 does not (3.05:1 dark).
effect: In the ticket queue the 'Search tickets… (Enter)' placeholder renders at 2.22:1 dark / 2.43:1 light and reads as an almost-empty box; the same happens to the folder-name, image-URL and per-page placeholders in the KB and Appearance modals. Fails in both themes, so toggling the theme does not fix it — but it does not affect the other ~164 inputs.

title: KPI stat-card labels use --text-pale, whose contrast RANK inverts between modes
evidence: {label}
fix: Replace `var(--text-pale)` with `var(--text-3)` here (dark 6.56:1, light 7.24:1 on --bg-card; 6.23:1 / 6.15:1 on --bg-hover) so the label holds AA in both modes and through the hover transition. Same change at lines 231 and 235.
effect: On the dashboard landing screen in light mode the six KPI tile captions (OPEN, UNASSIGNED, …) render mid-grey #64748b at 11px/uppercase/0.14em and look visibly washed out next to the same labels in dark mode; hovering a tile drops them to 3.86:1, below AA.

title: Home StatCard label repeats the --text-pale rank inversion
evidence: {label}
fix: Replace with `var(--text-3)` for the label. Since --text-pale has only 5 usages app-wide and duplicates --text-4 exactly in light mode, consider retiring the token rather than patching each site.
effect: On the home screen in light mode the eight stat-tile captions look duller than their dark-mode counterparts, but remain legible (4.55:1) — a theme-parity polish issue, not unreadable text.

title: Profile detail-row labels use --text-5 on --bg-card
evidence: {label}
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` for the label (6.56:1 dark / 7.24:1 light on --bg-card). Note globals.css:232 already defines `.label { color: var(--text-3) }` as the house style for form labels — this component diverges from it by two ramp steps.
effect: On a user profile page, in both dark and light mode, the 10px uppercase field captions (EMPLOYEE ID, REPORTS TO, BUSINESS IMPACT) are barely visible against the card, so those three values appear as three unlabelled strings.

title: All 12 edit-form <label> elements use --text-5
evidence: <label style={{ display: 'block', fontSize: 10, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-5)', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.08em', marginBottom: 5 }}>
fix: Replace `var(--text-5)` with `var(--text-3)` in all 12 label declarations, matching the `.label` helper already defined at globals.css:229-232.
effect: In the Edit Profile and Change Password modals, in both themes, all 12 field captions (FIRST NAME, EMAIL, EMPLOYEE ID, ROLE, STATUS, CURRENT PASSWORD…) render near-invisible at 10px against the modal surface, so the form is a column of unlabelled boxes and the theme toggle appears to do nothing.

title: Recent-tickets table column headers use --text-5 while globals.css uses --text-3 for the same role
evidence: <th key={h} style={{ padding: '8px 16px', textAlign: 'left', fontSize: 10, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-5)', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.07em' }}>
fix: Change to `var(--text-3)` to match `.data-table thead th`, or apply the `.data-table` class and drop the inline header styles entirely.
effect: On the user profile page in both themes, the Recent Tickets table appears to have no column headers — a visible inconsistency against every other table in the app, which renders headers at ~7:1.

title: Ticket-list data values ('Unassigned', '—') rendered at --text-5
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` for these values (6.56:1 dark / 7.24:1 light on --bg-card). If 'Unassigned' is meant to read as a warning rather than a null, it warrants a semantic accent instead of a ramp step.
effect: On the ticket queue in both themes, the italic 'Unassigned' in the Assigned To column and the '—' placeholders in Level/Group/SLA are so faint they read as empty cells, and they fade further (2.11:1 dark / 2.06:1 light) on the row the user is hovering.

title: 'Created' and 'Client/Org' ticket-list columns use --text-4: 3.53:1 dark (FAIL) vs 4.55:1 light (pass)
fix: Either raise these call sites to `var(--text-3)`, or fix the token: redefine dark `--text-4` to roughly #8595a8 so it clears 4.5:1 on --bg-card, which repairs all 417 --text-4 usages at once.
effect: On the ticket queue the Created and Client/Org columns render grey-on-grey in dark mode (3.97:1) and only marginally better in light (4.31:1) — both under AA, and both degrade to ~3.4-3.9:1 on the hovered row.

title: Notification ticket ref and timestamp at --text-5 on --bg-deep
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` (7.36:1 dark / 6.39:1 light on --bg-deep) for the ticket ref and timestamp, and for the group header at line 143.
effect: In the notifications panel in both themes — worse in light — the ticket reference under each notification, the '2h ago' timestamps and the TODAY/YESTERDAY group headers are near-invisible, so the user cannot tell which ticket a notification is about without clicking it.

title: Read notifications drop their message text to --text-4: 3.97:1 dark, below AA
fix: Use `var(--text-2)` for read notifications (12.77:1 dark / 8.73:1 light on --bg-deep). The unread emphasis is already carried by fontWeight 600 vs 400 (line 172) and the background tint on line 158, so the color step can be much gentler.
effect: In the notifications panel, already-read notification messages sit just under AA (3.97:1 dark / 4.01:1 light) — noticeably dimmer than unread ones but still readable; no mode-dependent difference.

title: 'COMING SOON' badge pairs --text-5 with --bg-elevated — 1.91:1 dark
evidence: <div style={{ position: 'absolute', top: 14, right: 14, fontSize: 9, fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-5)', background: 'var(--bg-elevated)', border: '1px solid var(--border-subtle)', padding: '2px 7px', letterSpacing: '0.1em' }}>
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` on --bg-elevated (5.65:1 dark / 6.74:1 light). Any --text-5 text on --bg-elevated should be treated as a hard error in this system.
effect: On the KB landing page in both themes, the COMING SOON badge on the Documentation tile is illegible at 9px, but the tile is already visibly greyed at 0.55 opacity and non-clickable, so no state information is actually lost.

title: KB landing body copy uses --text-4: 3.53:1 dark, fails AA for the page's main descriptive text
fix: Body prose should use `var(--text-2)` (11.37:1 dark / 9.90:1 light on --bg-card) or at minimum `var(--text-3)`. Reserve --text-4 for timestamps and disabled affordances only, and only after the dark value is corrected.
effect: On the KB landing page in dark mode, the hero subtitle and each tile's description paragraph render dull grey at 3.53-3.97:1 against much brighter headings — the 'dull fonts in dark mode' pattern; in light mode they are 4.31-4.55:1, i.e. borderline.

title: Calendar weekday header letters (M T W T F S S) use --text-5
evidence: {l}
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` (6.56:1 dark / 7.24:1 light). Axis labels are navigational, not decorative, and should sit at or above the --text-3 step.
effect: On the calendar page in both themes, the M T W T F S S row above the sidebar mini date-picker is effectively blank, so the user has to count columns to know which weekday a date cell is.

title: Sidebar section headings at --text-5 are DIMMER than the --text-3 list items they label
evidence: STATUS
fix: Raise both headings to `var(--text-3)` or `var(--text-2)` so the label is at least as prominent as its contents.
effect: On the calendar page in both themes, the STATUS and THIS WEEK group headings in the left sidebar recede almost to invisibility while the items beneath them stay bright, so the sidebar reads as unlabelled fragments.

title: Ticket-header copy buttons use --text-5 — an interactive control below the 3:1 UI floor
evidence: style={{ color: copied === 'ref' ? '#34d399' : 'var(--text-5)', background: 'none', border: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', padding: '2px 4px', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', flexShrink: 0 }}
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` for idle icon-button color (6.56:1 dark / 7.24:1 light on --bg-card), matching the `.icon-btn` helper at globals.css:224 which already specifies `color: var(--text-3)`.
effect: On the ticket detail page in both themes the two copy icons next to the ticket reference are invisible until hovered, and the surrounding --text-5 metadata ('Resolution Note', 'No messages in this ticket.', article byline, time-log dates) is barely readable.

title: .btn-ghost, .pagination-btn and .empty-state-text all use --text-4
fix: Correct the dark `--text-4` value (globals.css:56) from #64748b to roughly #8595a8, which lifts it to ~4.6:1 on --bg-card and repairs these helpers plus all 417 inline --text-4 usages simultaneously. This is the single highest-leverage fix for the reported dark-mode dullness.
effect: 'View all' / 'New Announcement' ghost buttons and the pagination arrows render at 3.5-4:1 and look semi-disabled in dark mode; in light mode they improve only to ~4.3-4.6:1, so they stay marginal rather than becoming correct.

title: Canned-response category headers use --text-5 on an explicit --bg-surface
evidence:
color: 'var(--text-5)', textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.08em',
                    borderBottom: '1px solid var(--border-subtle)',
                    background: 'var(--bg-surface)',
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` (6.91:1 dark / 7.58:1 light on --bg-surface) for group headers, consistent with `.panel-title` (globals.css:180-183) which uses --text-2 for the same role.
effect: While searching canned responses in the reply composer, the category grouping headers above each result cluster are near-invisible in both themes, so search hits look like one undifferentiated list; the non-search browse view is unaffected.

title: Completed to-dos and announcement metadata drop to --text-5
fix: Use `var(--text-4)` plus `textDecoration: 'line-through'` for the completed state — strikethrough carries the semantics without pushing contrast below AA. Metadata at lines 318/335/492/493 should be --text-3.
effect: On the home screen in both themes, a to-do you tick fades to ~2.3-2.5:1 and its struck-through text becomes hard to read (worse on hover at ~2.1:1); announcement author/date lines are similarly faint on the announcement cards.

title: Two sibling label styles on one screen use different ramp steps
fix: Unify both on `var(--text-3)`. Establish one token for the uppercase micro-label role rather than picking a ramp step per component.
effect: On a user profile page the four stat-tile captions (OPEN, RESOLVED, CLOSED, TOTAL) and the field captions immediately below them render at visibly different brightness in both themes, so the page looks like two label systems collided; in dark mode both are under AA.
